## Objective
- Build a complete playable game, then adapt it into a more realistic, full-3D-style jumping spider adventure spanning multiple environments.

## Requirements
- User wants a jumping spider protagonist that starts in a tree and learns jumping, climbing, webbing, attacking, and eating bugs for health or power-ups.
- Progress through the garden, sandbox, lawn, kitchen, bedroom, and bathroom; use stage hazards in boss fights.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Replaced the initial Starwell concept with “Little Legs,” a seven-stage adventure.
- Implemented the visuals as a canvas-based 2D game with layered depth and environmental scenery; it is not a true 3D world.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added game title screen, HUD, responsive styling, keyboard and touch control markup.
- Implemented canvas scenery, spider drawing, bugs, platforms, web projectiles, bosses, hazards, health, scoring, and stage progression in code.

### Active
- Finish and verify the game implementation; confirm gameplay works across all seven stages and responsive touch controls.
- Reconcile the requested “full 3D world” with the current 2D canvas approach or improve the visual depth accordingly.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect `game.js` for syntax/runtime issues and test locally in a browser.
2. Fix gameplay/control bugs and check stage progression and boss/hazard encounters.
3. Capture and inspect a current small JPEG screenshot; improve visuals and mobile layout as needed.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Little Legs game structure, title screen, HUD, controls.
- `style.css`: game styling, responsive and touch-control layouts.
- `game.js`: canvas rendering, game state, input, mechanics, stages, bosses.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; no tests, browser check, or screenshot have been performed.
- Game uses a 960×600 canvas and seven stages; `game.js` is the primary unfinished implementation.

- Finish the existing game as a complete, playable jumping-spider adventure across varied environments.
- Improve visual realism and depth; the user said a full 3D world “would be cool.”

## Requirements
- Start in a tree and teach jumping, climbing, webbing, attacking, and eating bugs for health or power-ups.
- Progress through the garden, sandbox, lawn, kitchen, bedroom, and bathroom; use stage hazards in boss fights.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.
- Check screenshots using a small JPEG at a viewport no wider than 1280px; read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- The game is titled “Little Legs” and has seven stages, three boss encounters, and a jumping-spider protagonist.
- The current implementation is a 2D canvas game with layered scenery, not a full 3D world.

## Work State
### Completed
- Replaced the earlier Starwell page with Little Legs markup and responsive styling.
- Implemented canvas rendering, spider and bug visuals, movement, jumping, climbing, web attacks, bites, snacks, health, hazards, bosses, stage progression, pause, sound, and touch controls in `game.js`.

### Active
- Verify syntax, runtime behavior, controls, stage progression, boss fights, and mobile layout.
- Assess visual quality and whether to improve depth toward the requested full-3D feel.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect `game.js` for syntax/runtime issues and test locally in a browser.
2. Exercise all seven stages, progression conditions, boss/hazard encounters, and keyboard/touch controls; fix any issues.
3. Save and inspect a current small JPEG screenshot; improve visuals and mobile layout as needed.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Little Legs game structure, title screen, HUD, controls.
- `style.css`: game styling, responsive and touch-control layouts.
- `game.js`: canvas rendering, input, mechanics, stages, bosses, hazards.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; no tests, browser check, or screenshot have been performed.

- Finish “Little Legs” as a playable seven-stage spider adventure, fix simultaneous movement and action controls, and make each stage progress through multiple areas instead of one room.

## Requirements
- Teach jumping, climbing, webbing, attacking, and eating bugs for health or power-ups.

- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.
- Check screenshots using a small JPEG at a viewport no wider than 1280px; read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- The game is a 2D canvas adventure with seven stages, three boss encounters, and layered scenery.
- Each stage now has three areas, with bug-snack goals and checkpoint gates between them.
- Bosses pursue the spider toward hazards rather than being held at a distant fixed clamp.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game structure, visuals, movement, combat, snacks, health, hazards, bosses, stage progression, pause, sound, and touch controls.
- Added three-area progression scaffolding to `seedStage`: 2100-unit stages, per-area snack goals, checkpoint platforms, and boss placements near the final area.
- Added checkpoint visuals, area HUD status, area-boundary gating, and per-area snack tracking.
- Started replacing shared touch-action state with per-source action-hold tracking.

### Active
- Finish and verify input handling: wire `actionHolds` into keyboard, canvas, and touch actions; remove global pointer-up cancellation; ensure joystick movement remains active during simultaneous actions.
- Test and refine multi-area progression, snack gates, checkpoints, boss fights, stage transitions, and survivability.
- Run syntax/browser checks and inspect only the latest screenshot at the specified viewport.

- (none)

3. Verify keyboard/touch combinations, syntax, browser behavior, win/lose states, and the latest screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: gameplay, stage/area generation and progression, boss logic, and input handling.
- `index.html`: game UI, HUD, and touch controls.
- `style.css`: responsive layout and touch-control styling.

- Changes are uncommitted; earlier `git status --short` showed `game.js`, `index.html`, and `style.css` as untracked.
